recipes.name: Antipasto Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (6 ounce) can black olives, drained and chopped
1 (.7 ounce) package dry Italian-style salad dressing mix
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Make the salad: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add shell pasta and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 9 minutes. Drain, run under cold water to cool pasta, and drain again.

Transfer drained pasta to a large bowl. Add Asiago, salami, pepperoni, tomatoes, bell peppers, and olives. Sprinkle dry dressing mix over top and stir until ingredients are thoroughly mixed. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Make the dressing: Whisk oil, vinegar, oregano, parsley, Parmesan, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl. Cover and set aside until ready to serve.
When ready to serve, pour dressing over chilled salad and mix until well combined.

raw_recipe.headline: Antipasto Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This antipasto pasta salad is perfect for parties, potlucks, and picnics! A delicious combo of pasta, meat, and cheese, it's hearty and so easy to make.

review.reviewBody: I made this for my step-daughters grad party and total strangers asked me for the recipe. I have to admit I didnt taste any at the party, but the next day I ate some leftovers and it was fantastic. I made a few alterations; rotini instead of sea shell, yellow or red pepper in place of green, 3oz. can of olives, 3 green onions, and instead of the dressing provided in the recipe- I used Newman's Own Light Balsamic Vinegrette. It was a huge hit. The key was to mix everything together but the balsamic dressing and let it sit for a while. In my case, 24 hours before I poured the Newman's Own on it. Really yummy! One reviewer suggested Pepperchini's, which I think would be a great addition. I didnt think this cost much to make, and I dont understand why people think there is so much chopping. That is a part of cooking! This is an excellent recipe and one woman at our party said it was going to be her pasta salad recipe from now on. Excellent! (Edited 5/9/2010)

Really good. There was not a bite left after the cookout. I used fussili pasta, I used halved grape tomatoes. I added chopped artichokes, I omitted the pepperoni and doubled the salami, I used a combination of brine cured olives, I added finely sliced red onion, I roasted the red peppers, omitted the oregano and used fresh parsley. Per the suggestion of a couple other reviewers, I used a little less oil, but I think I will use all of it next time. I liked the asiago cheese, but I think next time I will try real mozzarella instead. I will certainly make this again.

I followed advice and used Paul Newman’s dressing, added pepperoncini, green onions, cherry tomatoes. Still added half Packet of dry Italian dressing. I made one batch for my ladies meeting at church using the colored tortellini. And I used the shells for a get together at work for second batch. I would use the mini shells and not the regular shells next time. Adding all the extra vegetables made the batches bigger. I had to send home food with people and still had leftovers. So the 12 servings are very large servings. Everyone loved it and several people asked for the recipe.

This is a new favorite summer salad. Altered it some by decreasing the evoo to 1/2 cup and upping the balsamic to a 1/2 cup. I didn't serve it right away. I let it sit overnight as I do with all my pasta salads so that the pasta can absorb the dressing completely. Can you say WINNER!!! I kept going in the fridge myself sneaking forkfuls. I also didn't add the parmesan as they stated to the dressing. I added it after the dressing and mixed it altogether. What flavor! And the asiago - I love asiago. If you take it out of the recipe, you're missing something wonderful. Asiago adds a certain kind of flavor one just can't describe, that's why you have taste buds.

I used tricolor rotini, and havarti and gouda cheese instead of asiago. I also let the pasta salad sit in the Italian dressing mix for 2 hours, added the oil, balsamic vinegar and spices but for my preference, it needed to marinade overnight or longer for all the flavors to marry together. It is really good, love the flavor the balsamic vinegar adds. Will definitely make again.
I use Newman's own balsamic vinaigrette and let marinate overnight. Otherwise exactly as written and has become a family request.

This is primarily this recipe with some alterations of my own and my mother's "dressing" which is just a low oil variation on Good Season's Italian dressing mix recipe. I let this dry marinade overnight after mixing the vegetables, noodles, meat, and cheeses with the single packet of Good Season's Italian dressing mix, just the dry mix. I did add a tablespoon of oregano and a teaspoon of parsley, it's a mild but noticeable punch in the flavor of just the dressing mix packets by themselves, specifically the oregano but not overpowering. The following day, I do the dressing and final mix. I'm sure you can do it all in one day, I just usually do most of the work the night before, so it's just ready to go. My mother's dressing recipe is the low oil alternative on the instructions on the packet. She uses Apple Cider Vinegar instead of Balsamic Vinegar and two packets of sweetener per 1 packet of dry dressing mix. I usually make 16ozs of dressing for 2 boxes of 12oz Tricolor Rotini Pasta. But 16ozs is too much for a standard 16oz box of other types of pasta, so reserve some to "rehydrate" the salad if you're eating it over the course of multiple days, as the noodles will suck up all the water and veer towards drying. I put in regular Havarti and Havarti with dill this time, in addition to Parmesan and two handfuls of mozzarella. I also crush some Italian croutons in a Ziploc bag and put those on and stir as the final step before eating. Oh, and some diced ham. I used to always make an antipasto salad like this for potlucks and picnics as it was requested.

I will be making this again...didn't have the same pasta the recipe called for but I think any bite-sized pasta will always work. Also, as somewhat of a traditionalist, I used Mediterranean olives (Greek, Kalamata, and Spanish Green) instead of canned black olives, marinated artichoke hearts, grilled red peppers, 1/2 cup quartered cucumber, and about 1/4 cup of red onion chopped. I also used shaved and grated parmesan cheese as I had that on hand but will make it in the future with delicious Asiago! HINT: If you save jars to pour used oil into, use one of them to make the dressing ... way neater and easier to blend!

I made this today for a Super Bowl party & had to sample it. Love it! I used grape tomatoes, at someone else’s suggestion, perfect! I made this in the morning, except for the dressing. I made the dressing in the afternoon and used a cruet to mix well. Will add the dressing right before leaving today.

It's super easy and delicious. This is also an excellent recipe for riffing; feel free to add anything else good on an Italian sub. I've had great luck with small hot pepper rings, different types of olives and salami, thin onion strands, and even prosciutto ribbons. I generally use about a full pound each of meat and cheese and try to make sure they complement each other. Last potluck, I used asiago, mozzarella pearls, genoa, capicola, and a little prosciutto; it was amazing! Also, if you want the salad to stay fresh a little longer, consider substituting small whole olives and grape tomatoes for chopped ones (the multi-colored varieties look beautiful in this salad). It will minimize the amount of the salad that liquifies over time.
A big hit every time I take it anywhere. For those that eat low carb I substitute the pasta for cauliflower cut into bite sized pieces and steamed. Those that are not low carb even like it.

Pretty good but studying the ingredients list I noticed a lack of red onion which I think needed to be added. I did not have enough Asiago cheese so I added fresh whole milk mozzarella and a bit of sharp cheddar and also added some smoked polish kielbasa. This was after I made the dish to the ' T ' and felt it was a bit bland.I would not normally add or switch ingredients in a recipe until.at.least trying it . And I did, and you know the rest.

I used 2 pkg Good seasons dressing- my salad was large because I used a lot of cheese and vegetables! I did not use Asiago due to personal preference- used provolone. I took the suggestion to use Paul Newmans Balsamic dressing and added the peppercini- this was very good Italian pasta salad!! Will definitely make again!! Delicious!!
Used Rotini pasta. Didn't have any salami. Also used white cheddar cheese because it's what I had on hand. Very good dressing!
I thought this was great, but my family didn't. Next time I'll skip the tomatoes.
Made for Super Bowl, it was a big hit!
